change: multi-anchor TTA: score the SAME trained model at A-0..A-29, subtract realised gmv over [A-k+1,A], recombine (666 weighting/smoothing/combiner schemes)
notes: TEST-TIME ONLY; training byte-identical to e0101 and the k=0 column reproduces e0101's folds EXACTLY, so the comparison is paired. NOT ONE of 666 schemes beats k=0; LOFO scheme selection picks k0 on all 5 folds, honest gain +0.00000. The proposal as stated (subtract+rescale, linear weights, log space) is a DISASTER: cal 1.76358 -> 2.07297, rho 0.66162 -> 0.47243. Two causes. (1) Unit mismatch: expm1(model) estimates ~E[log1p y], g_k is an arithmetic realised sum -- mean g_29 = 93.1 vs mean p_29 = 38.0, so 42.9% of users clip to zero. This is the +0.5626 functional gap of EXPERIMENTS.md 1e. (2) Anchor shift is NOT label-preserving: anchor A-k predicts window [A-k+1, A-k+30], a DIFFERENT target, so averaging adds bias linear in k while the variance saved is ~0 (adjacent anchors correlate >0.99). Pure averaging with NO subtraction also loses (+0.00015 best). Internal check: uniform_2/extrap == k0 to 8 dp, as the algebra requires. See EXPERIMENTS.md 1n.

notes: P2 REFUTED, PRE-REGISTERED (I gave the null 75/25 and it holds). The better ranker makes the product worse. WHY: RMSLE elicits E[L|x] and the hurdle identity E[L|x]=P(buy|x)*E[L|x,buy] multiplies two separately-estimated halves, so errors compound; the magnitude half is trained on a population (buyers) that is NOT the scoring population, and its calibration on the 43% zeros is undefined -- it predicts 3.763 there. change: The e0243 magnitude prediction AS A FEATURE (stacked, OOF-honest) instead of as a multiplicand -- the open route left by e0245

(1) RESIDUAL SCREEN on the real 5-fold OOF (1q method, zero training): corr(mag_pred, baseline residual) = +0.0047 on the FULL population, incremental R2 = 0.00003 vs the 0.0002 kill bar. A LOFO refit of L on [1, base, mag] -- an upper bound on any linear use -- scores 1.76538 vs 1.76515 baseline = +0.00023 WORSE. A fully non-parametric 20x20 2-D map of (base,mag) is +0.00564 worse. (2) LIGHTGBM STACK on the local harness with pipeline params AND early stopping (the 1r lesson): -0.00002 mean, better in 4/9 runs, against a NOISE-COLUMN control at +0.00021, better in 3/9. INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A RANDOM COLUMN. WHY THE +0.0575 DOES NOT TRANSFER, which is the durable finding: corr(mag, base) = +0.8747 overall and +0.8957 among buyers -- the magnitude model is ~88% redundant with the baseline it would be stacked on. And among buyers corr(mag, baseline residual) = -0.4152, i.e. the WRONG SIGN for a stack: the baseline OVER-predicts exactly where the magnitude model says 'high', because among buyers base ~ P(buy)*amount, so a high base can mean 'certain to buy' rather than 'will spend a lot'. CONCLUSION: I13's magnitude gap is real (80.2% -> 89.8% of ceiling, e0243) but is NOT SPENDABLE by either route -- not as a multiplicand (e0245, +0.00462) and not as a feature (this row). Three independent kills of the hurdle decomposition (e0010, e0237, e0245) plus one of stacking. EXPERIMENTS.md 1u.

Measured directly: predictions on zero-target users inflate 1.4059 -> 1.8752 -> 2.5002 for w=1/2/5 and overall bias goes +0.1402 -> +0.5300 -> +0.9909. RMSLE pays for that immediately. Consistent with 1q: the model is already within 0.0010 of E[L|M], so any re-weighting moves it AWAY from the right estimand. THE DIAGNOSTIC, THIRD OCCURRENCE: at w=5 corr(L,.|Z=1) RISES +0.0085 (0.4623 -> 0.4708) while RMSLE DEGRADES +0.29161. The magnitude statistic and the competition metric move in OPPOSITE directions -- the same dissociation as e0243 (+0.0575 magnitude, nothing end-to-end) and e0245 (better magnitude half, worse product).
